title: The hun and the p'o
summary: The Chinese teaching of two souls.

claims.text: Chinese belief holds that each person has two souls: the hun, made at conception, governs mind and spirit, and the p'o, made at birth, governs the body; like yin and yang they cannot work apart.
At death they part, and the p'o stays near the corpse to guard it and see that proper funeral rites are done.

title: Qin Shihuang and the Ways of the Spirits
summary: The First Emperor's search for immortality.

claims.text: Late in life Qin Shihuang became obsessed with escaping death and kept mystics and magicians at court; when they failed, the emperor turned on them in fury.
Then a group came claiming to follow an old magical tradition called the Ways of the Spirits, rumored to hold power in both this world and the land of the dead.

title: The storm after Hiroshima
summary: How the atomic bombings struck the Jade Kingdom.

claims.text: The atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki unleashed a great Maelstrom through every realm of the dead. The Jade Kingdom spent weeks sheltering in Haunts and manor houses.
The storm tore up stretches of the Imperial Highway from the Yellow Springs to the Jade Palace and badly damaged most Imperial buildings.
Peng Xin, hero of the war with Stygia, was earlier made a minister by the Emperor in place of the vanished Wu.

title: The Jade militia
summary: How the Dark Kingdom of Jade raises soldiers.

claims.text: Local Commanders oversee training and the district armory, since most weapons are banned to citizens; monthly drills are required by law but seldom held.
Families may legally buy off militia duty for a yearly fee by showing hardship, and many Commanders define hardship loosely; the professional regiments are volunteers.

title: Ti Yu, the Earth Prison
summary: The hells of the Jade Kingdom.

claims.text: The hells were built around an underground walled city named Ti Yu, the Earth Prison, with broad streets and a Hall of Justice; like the Jade Palace and Stygia it lies within the Tempest.

Its cavern entrance at the mountain of Feng-tu and the maze beneath resemble the Veinous Stair; Hell is the harshest sentence of Jade law, but its capacity is limited, so the flow of souls into it is kept in check.
